rationale: I'm replacing the Pearson/Fisher-z features with a tangent-space embedding of Ledoit-Wolf shrunk correlation matrices, keeping the CC200 atlas and the classifier unchanged. Abraham 2017 found this to be the strongest classic connectivity measure for ABIDE. It respects the geometry of covariance matrices, and the shrinkage keeps all-zero ROIs from making the matrices singular. The reference mean is the log-Euclidean mean over all items, which uses no labels.

I'm adding per-site mean-centering of the tangent-space features before the global scaler and the logistic regression. The site means are computed over the train and test items from each site together, using no labels. ABIDE scanner and protocol offsets are large, so the classifier currently spends capacity on between-site variance that is pure noise for within-site AUROC; removing it should sharpen the within-site autism signal. I left C=0.001 as it was and did no inner-CV tuning this round. I don't know the exact format of `ctx["meta_train"]`, so the code reads the site labels defensively and skips centering if it can't find them.

I'm replacing the single CC200 model with an ensemble of tangent-space logistic regressions over four parcellations: CC200, CC400, Harvard-Oxford and AAL. Each atlas gets its own scaler, and C is scaled by 1/(number of features) so all four are regularized about as strongly as the CC200 model that worked. The test-set probabilities from the four models are averaged. Abraham 2017 found that the choice of parcellation matters a lot on ABIDE, and these atlases split the brain differently: data-driven versus anatomical, at coarse and fine resolution. Their connectome errors should be partly independent, so averaging them should cut variance in this p >> n setting.

I'm replacing the hand-fixed C=0.001 with a C chosen by grouped inner 3-fold CV on the training fold, using `groups_train`. Inner folds are scored by within-site AUROC, the same metric as the harness. In this p >> n tangent-space regime the classifier is very sensitive to regularization strength, and the best C should depend on the training data rather than being guessed. The features are unchanged.

I'm adding a second CC200 tangent-space model built on the global-signal-regressed time series (`filt_global`) and averaging its log-odds with the current no-GSR model. GSR changes the correlation structure a lot: it removes shared physiological and motion noise and shifts correlations toward anti-correlations. Whether it helps autism classification is disputed, so two views of the same parcellation should have partly independent errors that averaging can cancel. Round 3's ensemble varied the atlas and gained only +0.0001; this one varies the preprocessing instead.

Correlation-based tangent features standardize each ROI, so they throw away regional fluctuation amplitude. Autism shows altered amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF), and the series are already band-pass filtered, so each ROI's log standard deviation works as an ALFF proxy. This change appends a 200-feature ALFF block to the tangent features. Each subject's amplitudes are taken relative to their own whole-brain mean, which removes global scale and motion effects. Each ROI is then z-scored within site, using site labels only to harmonize. The block is up-weighted so it isn't drowned out by the 20k edge features.

I'm reweighting the training samples so that autism and control count equally within each site (weight = n_site / (2·n_site,class), normalized to mean 1). Site prevalence then no longer correlates with diagnosis in training. Without this, the logistic regression can use part of its tightly regularized budget on scanner and site signatures that track each site's case ratio. Those signatures are useless for within-site AUROC and pull the weight vector away from the true connectivity signal. Site is used only to reweight samples, never as a feature. Features, C and the scaler are unchanged.

I'm adding split-half data augmentation in the tangent space and leaving the features and the classifier alone. Each subject also gets two extra connectomes, one from each half of their time series. The logistic regression trains on the full connectome plus both halves, with weights that sum to one per subject, and it predicts from the full connectome only. Within-subject connectome sampling noise is large and differs by site, because scan length and TR vary. Showing the model the same subject's label under that noise should make it ignore noisy edge directions and focus on stable trait connectivity. That would act as a regularizer matched to the data, without changing C.

I'm replacing the per-edge StandardScaler with a single global scale factor. The tangent features are centred, then divided by the root of the mean feature variance, so total variance matches the current setup and C=0.001 regularizes about as strongly as before. Z-scoring each of the ~20k edges inflates low-variance edges that are mostly noise, such as near-constant edges from all-zero or out-of-field-of-view ROIs. Keeping the natural tangent-space metric instead lets the L2 penalty favour the high-variance connectivity directions that carry subject traits, which acts like a PCA-style prior. This also matches how Abraham 2017 fed tangent vectors to linear classifiers.

I'm replacing the single global tangent reference point with a per-site Riemannian re-centering, following Riemannian Procrustes re-centering (Zanini 2018). Each subject's matrix is whitened by the log-Euclidean mean of its own site before the log map. The site means are label-free, built from that site's train and test items together. Round 2 subtracted each site's mean from the finished tangent features, which is a linear shift after the log map. This change instead moves each site's whole cloud of connectivity matrices onto the identity before the log map. That should also remove the scanner- and protocol-dependent distortions of the covariance shape (different scan length, TR and shrinkage level), not just their offset. If no site labels can be read, the code falls back to the current global log-Euclidean reference.

I'm adding DVARS-based scrubbing before the Ledoit-Wolf/tangent pipeline. DVARS is the RMS frame-to-frame signal change across the standardized ROIs. Frames on either side of a transition whose DVARS is above a robust outlier threshold (median + 3·MAD) are dropped, capped at 25% of frames. Head-motion spikes inflate short-range correlations and flatten long-range ones, and the ABIDE pipeline gives us no censoring or motion covariates. Removing those frames should make each subject's covariance reflect trait connectivity rather than session-specific artefacts. Everything else is unchanged: atlas, tangent reference, scaler and C.
